newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares, unfased by a lower-than-expected reserves figure, climbed to their fifth consecutive closing high fuelled by gains in heavyweight stock Richemont.
But the gold index slid, dragged down by bullion which fixed at a fresh 4 -1/4 year low.

Dealers said arbitrage trading between spot shares and the futures market, which roared ahead on Tuesday welcoming the milestone relaxation of foreign exchange controls on individuals on that day, lifted several key industrial index stocks.
Gains on the bond and rand markets were further boons.
"The (reserves) figures weren't great but you have to take into account that a lot of banks held onto their reserves in June ahead of the easing of foreign exchange controls," a dealer said.
"If anything, the market was pleased by the way the rand handled the easing of (forex) controls and people are happy that they can take money overseas."
Since Tuesday individuals can invest a once-off 200,000 rand offshore.

Hungry buying out of Switzerland and demand for rand hedge stocks pushed Richemont to yet another 1997 best at 71 rand as some worries remained that the rand may weaken if flows offshore picked up and as local investors responded positively to a roadshow by management.
"Richemont is a big rand hedge stock but also its results in Swiss franks were pretty good," said Paul Nettleton of Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.

Richemont last Thursday posted a 4.2 percent drop in attributable year profit to 302.9 million sterling but said the results were impacted by the strength of sterling and deeper losses in its media interests. Its core tobacco and luxury goods businesses, however, achieved satisfactory growth, it said.
The industrial index finished up 23.8 points at 8,832.5 as the near-month futures contract held at 8,678/85 from 8,678.

Gold shares slipped as bullion continued to hover weakly at around the $332 level as as funds positioned themselves to take advantage of prices falling further and this induced gold producers in especially high cost areas like Australia to step up their selling programmes.
The index ended down 3.9 points at 964.7 and the September gold futures contract was last at 680/700 from 682.
Engineering firm Murray & Roberts was busy again, ending two cents weaker at 898 cents after it warned on Tuesday that it would report a loss in year earnings after certain once-off charges.

Food group Premier rose 20 cents to 680 cents following a bookover trade in 1.5 million shares. Premier last week reported a 32 percent jump in year headline earnings to 38.0 cents a share -- in line with expectations.
Overall the all-share index finished off 3.4 points at 7,416.7 as decliners outpaced advancers by 209 to 159.
Data released late on Tuesday showed that South Africa held 22.1 billion rand's worth of gold and foreign exchange reserves in June, well below economists' expectations of 24.68 billion.
